title: OmniVia Core Application Contract v1 - chat payloads
description: Input and result payloads for the two chat application operations. Chat's own command, query, event and generation vocabularies are published separately and in full as Chat Contract v1 (`contracts/chat/v1`); this document deliberately does not restate them. It binds what the *application* boundary owns -- which chat command is being settled, which conversation revision the caller expects it to apply to, and which generation stream is being replayed -- and carries the chat document itself as an opaque JSON object the application envelope neither inspects nor validates. Restating thirty command shapes here would create a second, drifting copy of a contract that is already frozen elsewhere; carrying them keeps one source for chat semantics and one source for application authority. This document declares no root type: it is a definition container only.

ChatConversationExpectation.title: ChatConversationExpectation
ChatConversationExpectation.description: The conversation a chat command changes, and the revision the caller believes it is at. Optimistic concurrency for the conversation aggregate, stated as both counters rather than one: a conversation's `graph_revision` and its append position move independently, so expecting only one of them admits a command whose view is stale in exactly the half it did not state. A mismatch is a `conflict` the caller re-reads and re-decides against; it is not a `mutation_precondition_failed`, which names a record version the caller refreshes and retries.

conversation_id.description: Identifier of the conversation this command expects to change.

graph_revision.description: The conversation graph's optimistic revision token as the caller last observed it.

latest_conversation_sequence.description: The conversation's latest append position as the caller last observed it.

ChatCommandInput.title: ChatCommandInput
ChatCommandInput.description: Input for `chat.command`: one Chat Contract v1 command, settled through the workspace's single mutation seam. `command_name` names a member of the Chat Contract's own closed command registry and `command` is that command's request document, carried verbatim and opaque to this envelope. Workspace-scoped through the request envelope's selected workspace, so this payload never carries a second, independent workspace identifier. The envelope's `idempotency_key` is required by the catalogue and is what makes a repeated submission answer from the settled outcome rather than appending a second message.

command_name.description: The Chat Contract v1 command name, such as `SubmitMessage`. Refused when it is not a member of that contract's closed registry.

command.description: The Chat Contract v1 request document for `command_name`, carried verbatim. Decoded and validated against the chat contract, never against this one.

expected_conversation.description: The conversation revision this command expects. Absent for a command that touches no existing conversation.

ChatCommandResult.title: ChatCommandResult
ChatCommandResult.description: Result of `chat.command`: the settled command's own Chat Contract v1 result envelope, echoed with the command name it answers. The chat result is carried opaquely for the same reason the request is. A replayed submission returns the stored result of the command that already ran, not a second settlement.

command_name.description: The Chat Contract v1 command name this result answers. Echoes the request.

command_result.description: The Chat Contract v1 `CommandResultEnvelope` the command produced, carried verbatim.

conversation_id.description: The conversation the settled command changed, where it changed one.

ChatGenerationEvent.title: ChatGenerationEvent
ChatGenerationEvent.description: One durable generation-lifecycle event, as the workspace recorded it. Provider content is never carried: `payload` holds only the sanitised, closed-vocabulary fields the workspace persisted, and no request body, response body, header, URL or credential has a path into it.

event_type.description: The durable event type, such as `chat.generation.started`. Open by design so a compatible minor release can add lifecycle vocabulary.

generation_event_sequence.description: This event's position in its generation's contiguous history, counting from one.

cursor.description: The server-issued cursor naming this position. Round-tripped verbatim as a later request's `after_cursor`; never parsed.

occurred_at.description: When the workspace recorded this event.

ChatEventsInput.title: ChatEventsInput
ChatEventsInput.description: Input for `chat.events`: replay one generation's durable event history after a cursor. A request carrying no `after_cursor` replays the whole history. Transport-level streaming is out of scope: this is a replay of what was recorded, not a subscription. Workspace-scoped through the request envelope's selected workspace, so this payload never carries a second, independent workspace identifier.

generation_job_id.description: Identifier of the generation whose events to replay.

after_cursor.description: Replay strictly after this position. Absent replays from the beginning.

ChatEventsResult.title: ChatEventsResult
ChatEventsResult.description: Result of `chat.events`: the durable event suffix after the requested cursor, or the demand for a fresh snapshot -- never both. When `requires_resnapshot` is true, `events` is empty and `resnapshot_reason` states why the requested position could not be honoured; a fabricated continuation is exactly what that answer exists to prevent. Events are strictly increasing, duplicate-free and contiguous from the position the request continued from.

generation_job_id.description: Identifier of the generation these events belong to. Echoes the request.

events.description: The durable events after the requested cursor, in ascending sequence order. Empty when a resnapshot is required.

requires_resnapshot.description: Whether the caller must take a fresh snapshot instead of continuing from the cursor it presented.

resnapshot_reason.description: Why a fresh snapshot is required, such as `cursor_unknown_or_expired`. Present only when `requires_resnapshot` is true.
